facts.spoken_summary: This is the NXP FRDM-MCXN236 development board, based on the Arm Cortex-M33 MCX N236 target MCU.
facts.value: The board is a development and evaluation platform based on one 32-bit Arm Cortex-M33 MCX N236 target MCU.

evidence.locator: Clock driver attachments for CTIMER0 through CTIMER4

facts.spoken_summary: Yes. The MCX N236 has five CTIMER instances, CTIMER0 through CTIMER4.
facts.value: The SDK exposes five CTIMER instances named CTIMER0, CTIMER1, CTIMER2, CTIMER3, and CTIMER4.

evidence.locator: Features and Table 1, MCXN236VDFT ordering information

facts.spoken_summary: U1 is the MCXN236VDFT: a 150-megahertz Cortex-M33 in a 184-pin VFBGA package with 1 megabyte of internal flash and 352 kilobytes of SRAM.
facts.value: The board schematic identifies U1 as MCXN236VDFT. The data sheet specifies this 184-pin VFBGA part with a 150 MHz Arm Cortex-M33, 1024 KB internal flash, and 352 KB SRAM.

evidence.locator: Communication Interfaces for Connectivity and Human-Machine Interfaces

facts.spoken_summary: The MCX N236 provides eight low-power Flexcomm blocks for SPI, I2C, or UART, two CAN FD controllers, two I3C controllers, high-speed USB, FlexIO, two SAI interfaces, and a digital microphone interface.
facts.value: Connectivity includes eight low-power Flexcomm blocks supporting SPI, I2C, or UART; high-speed host/device USB with PHY; two FlexCAN FD controllers; two I3C controllers; one FlexIO; two SAI interfaces; and a digital PDM microphone interface.

evidence.locator: Analog and General-purpose input/outputs feature lists

facts.spoken_summary: The MCXN236VDFT supports up to 106 GPIOs, two 16-bit ADCs, and two high-speed comparators.
facts.value: The MCXN236VDFT package supports up to 106 GPIOs. The device has two 16-bit ADCs supporting four parallel conversions, up to 2 Msps at 16 bits or 3.15 Msps at 12 bits, plus two high-speed comparators.

facts.spoken_summary: Yes. Besides five 32-bit CTIMERs, the MCX N236 has low-power, frequency-measurement, multi-rate, wake, micro-tick, OS-event, watchdog, and real-time-clock timers.
facts.value: The timer family includes five 32-bit asynchronous general-purpose timers/counters, a low-power timer, frequency-measurement timer, multi-rate timer, windowed watchdog timer, RTC with calendar, wake timer, micro-tick timer, and OS event timer.

facts.spoken_summary: The MCX N236 includes TrustZone, an EdgeLock Secure Enclave, a PUF-backed device identity, secure boot and update, cryptographic services, and authenticated debug lifecycle controls.
facts.value: Security includes Arm TrustZone, EdgeLock Secure Enclave Core Profile, AES-256, SHA-2, NIST P-256 ECC, TRNG, PUF-derived device identity, immutable secure boot, secure firmware update, key policies, attestation, and authenticated debug lifecycle management.

evidence.locator: CTIMER driver change log and APIs

facts.spoken_summary: The CTIMER driver supports reading the count, capture, match and compare control, and PWM setup.
facts.value: The board SDK provides CTIMER APIs for reading the timer count, capture values, match-channel reset and stop, edge capture, and PWM setup.

facts.spoken_summary: The board has a Winbond W25Q64JVSSIQ 64-megabit, or 8-megabyte, QSPI flash at U12.
facts.value: U12 is a 3 V Winbond W25Q64JVSSIQ 64-Mbit (8 MB) dual and quad SPI serial flash connected through Flexcomm 6.

facts.spoken_summary: The board has a 24 MHz target-system crystal, a 32.768 kHz RTC crystal, and a 16 MHz MCU-Link crystal.
facts.value: Y3 is a 24 MHz target-MCU reference crystal, Y2 is a 32.768 kHz RTC crystal, and Y1 is a 16 MHz MCU-Link crystal.

facts.spoken_summary: J11 is the target MCU USB 2.0 Type-C port and supports both host and device modes.
facts.value: The target MCU high-speed USB controller and PHY connect to J11, a USB 2.0 Type-C connector usable in host or device mode.

facts.spoken_summary: The board has two USB Type-C connectors: J11 for the target MCU and J10 for MCU-Link.
facts.value: Table 12 identifies two USB Type-C ports: target MCU USB at J11 and MCU-Link USB at J10.

facts.spoken_summary: The board uses CAN1 with the TJA1057 high-speed transceiver and exposes it on four-pin header J13.
facts.value: The target MCU has CAN0 and CAN1 controllers; the board routes CAN1 through TJA1057GTK/3Z at U11 to J13 with P5V0, CAN1_H, GND, and CAN1_L.

facts.spoken_summary: U10 is an FXLS8974CFR3 three-axis accelerometer on Flexcomm 2 I2C, with default 8-bit write address 0x30.
facts.value: U10 is an FXLS8974CFR3 3-axis low-g accelerometer connected over Flexcomm 2 I2C on P4_0 and P4_1; its default 8-bit write address is 0x30.

facts.spoken_summary: Q2 is an ambient-light phototransistor connected to target-MCU pin P0_25 for ADC evaluation.
facts.value: Q2 is an ALS-PT19-315C ambient-light phototransistor connected to P0_25 of the MCX N236 for ADC evaluation.

facts.spoken_summary: The board populates a digital PDM microphone at U7; the DA7212 codec and analog audio jacks are not populated by default.
facts.value: U7 is a populated SPK0641HT4H-1 PDM digital microphone. The DA7212 codec U6, headphone J14, and auxiliary input J21 are DNP.

facts.spoken_summary: The board provides Arduino and FRDM headers J1 through J4, mikroBUS sockets J5 and J6, Pmod J7, LCD FlexIO J8, and camera header J9.
facts.value: J1-J4 provide Arduino and FRDM expansion, J5-J6 are mikroBUS sockets, J7 is a DNP Pmod header, J8 is a 28-pin FlexIO LCD header, and J9 is a 32-pin camera header.

evidence.locator: Table 26 continuation, camera header pins 26 through 32

facts.spoken_summary: J9 is the 32-pin SmartDMA camera header; NXP tested it with OV7670, which uses pins 7 through 22.
facts.value: J9 is a 32-pin camera header carrying SmartDMA camera data, clock, sync, I2C, power, ground, and GPIO signals. The board manual says OV7670 uses pins 7 through 22.

evidence.locator: Sections 3.7 through 3.9, USB and bridge connections

facts.spoken_summary: The onboard MCU-Link supports SWD and SWO debug, VCOM USB-to-UART, and USBSIO USB-to-SPI or USB-to-I2C bridges.
facts.value: The LPC55S69-based MCU-Link provides SWD/SWO, a VCOM USB-to-UART bridge, USBSIO USB-to-SPI and USB-to-I2C bridges, and external-probe support.

facts.spoken_summary: SW1 resets the target MCU, SW2 is the active-low wakeup button on P0_20, and SW3 is the active-low ISP button on P0_6.
facts.value: SW1 is target reset, SW2 drives P0_20/WUU0_IN4 low for wakeup, and SW3 drives P0_6/ISPMODE_N low for ISP mode or general input.

facts.spoken_summary: D13 is the user RGB LED on P4_18, P4_19, and P4_17; D12 is reset status and D3 is 3.3-volt power status.
facts.value: D13 red, green, and blue connect to P4_18, P4_19, and P4_17. D12 indicates reset and D3 indicates the LDO_3V3 power rail.

facts.spoken_summary: The board uses a 5-volt input sourced from J11 target USB, J10 MCU-Link USB, or optional header J19, then generates its secondary rails.
facts.value: P5V0 can come from target USB J11, MCU-Link USB J10, or the optional J19 5 V header path; onboard regulators create LDO_3V3 and VDD_1V8.

facts.spoken_summary: The FRDM-MCXN236 board operating-temperature range is minus 40 to plus 105 degrees Celsius.
facts.value: The documented board operating-temperature range is -40 degrees C to +105 degrees C; the MCX N23x device supports up to 125 degrees C junction temperature.

facts.spoken_summary: Revision C and earlier boards with PMCXN236-marked parts may lack EdgeLock 2GO provisioning; MCXN236-marked parts contain the fix.
facts.value: The documented erratum says revision C and earlier PMCXN236-marked boards may not be provisioned for EdgeLock 2GO; the fix applies to MCXN236-marked parts.
